article_units.name: Design and Technology in Our World
article_units.subtitle: New and emerging technologies, energy, sustainability and smart materials

lessons.title: New and Emerging Technologies
lessons.description: Market pull, technology push, consumer choice and the impact of new technologies on industry and enterprise.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Expected close match to AQA Core Technical Principles lesson on new and emerging technologies. Core concepts (market pull/technology push, product life cycle, global production) are identical across boards. Reframe extended-response practice questions in Eduqas style (Q1-5 short answer + Q6 in-depth extended writing) and surface Eduqas examiner emphasis on specific justification rather than vague 'eco-friendly' claims. Specific AQA lesson cross-reference to be confirmed by content agent.

lessons.title: Sustainability and the 6 Rs
lessons.description: Rethink, reuse, recycle, repair, reduce, refuse. Life Cycle Analysis, carbon and ecological footprints.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: 6 Rs and Life Cycle Analysis are board-agnostic concepts. AQA D&T covers these identically. Adapt by replacing AQA-style 'evaluate' phrasing with Eduqas extended-writing prompts. Keep universal examples (mobile phones, packaging) but ensure no past-paper context is reused. Specific source lesson to be matched by content agent.

lessons.title: Energy Generation and Storage
lessons.description: Renewable and non-renewable sources, fossil fuel issues, energy storage for products and manufacturing.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Energy generation is universal physics content treated identically across all D&T boards. AQA D&T has a lesson covering the same renewable/non-renewable scope. High transfer — content agent should adapt examples and exam-style framing only.

lessons.title: Smart Materials and Modern Materials
lessons.description: SMA, polymorph, photo-chromic and thermo-chromic materials, electroluminescent film, QTC and composites.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Smart material definitions are universal. AQA D&T covers SMA, polymorph, thermo-chromic in the same depth. Eduqas spec is slightly broader on technical textiles (micro-encapsulation, biometrics, Rhovyl) — content agent must include these Eduqas-specific items if not in source. Flag any source-specific examples that need replacing.

lessons.title: Composites and Technical Textiles
lessons.description: Carbon fibre, Kevlar, GRP, geotextiles, micro-fibres, interactive and wearable textile electronics.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA D&T covers composites within a single smart-materials lesson; Eduqas gives technical textiles slightly heavier weighting (Rhovyl, geotextiles, interactive textiles named explicitly). Adapt the composite content from AQA but generate the technical-textiles half fresh from Eduqas amplification list.

lessons.title: CAD, CAM and Production Techniques
lessons.description: Advantages and disadvantages of CAD and CAM, plus CNC routing, laser cutting, 3D printing and embroidery applications.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: CAD/CAM advantages/disadvantages are universal. AQA covers in detail. Content agent should adapt directly, ensuring CNC routing, laser cutting and 3D printing are all explicitly named (Eduqas amplification lists these).

article_units.name: Electronic and Mechanical Systems
article_units.subtitle: Sensors, programmable components, motion, forces and mechanical calculations

lessons.title: Electronic Systems and the Input-Process-Output Model
lessons.description: Circuit and block diagrams, sensors, LDRs, thermistors, and the role of feedback in control systems.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Systems thinking (input/process/output) and sensor types are universal. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt content from AQA lesson on electronic systems. Surface Eduqas-specific examiner note: candidates lose marks for vague responses such as 'moisture sensor' without detail of detection mechanism.

lessons.title: Programmable Components and Microcontrollers
lessons.description: Microcontrollers and PICs, sub-routines, programmable interfacing and the benefits and limitations of reprogrammable systems.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Programmable component concepts are universal. AQA D&T covers PICs and microcontroller benefits/limitations. Content agent should adapt directly, keeping PIC and reprogrammability emphasis.

lessons.title: Mechanical Devices and Types of Motion
lessons.description: Rotary, linear, reciprocating and oscillating motion. Pulleys, gears, levers, cams, rack and pinion.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Types of motion and mechanical device classifications are board-agnostic. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt and surface Eduqas 2024 examiner finding: mechanical-device knowledge improved this year, students can access calculation questions well — practice questions should build on this momentum.

lessons.title: Mechanical Calculations: Levers, Gears and Pulleys
lessons.description: Velocity ratio, mechanical advantage, moments and worked examples of belt, pulley and gear systems.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA covers calculations but Eduqas is more procedural-heavy (explicit RV*dia formula, principle of moments, calculate-from-given-values). Content agent must work through Eduqas-style numerical worked examples with each formula stated explicitly. OCR misconception note: friction is not always undesirable — required for belt/pulley operation. Article format with embedded worked examples (no separate practice-format unit needed — too few marks in spec to justify it).

lessons.title: Forces, Stresses and Reinforcement
lessons.description: Tension, compression, torsion, shear and bending, plus how materials are reinforced and stiffened.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Forces and reinforcement methods are universal physics content. AQA D&T covers identically. Eduqas amplifies material-specific reinforcement (corrugating papers, laminating textiles, ribbing metals) — ensure all material areas are illustrated.

article_units.name: Materials and Their Properties
article_units.subtitle: Papers, boards, timbers, metals, polymers and textiles — sources, properties and stock forms

lessons.title: Papers and Boards
lessons.description: Paper categories, ISO sizes, gsm and microns, plus common papers and boards in everyday use.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Papers and boards content is largely identical across boards. AQA D&T has a dedicated paper/board lesson in the specialist material areas unit. Adapt directly. Eduqas requires gsm and micron units to be named — ensure they appear in worked examples and flashcards.

lessons.title: Natural and Manufactured Timbers
lessons.description: Hardwoods, softwoods and manufactured boards. Properties, defects and finishes.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Timber categories and named hardwoods/softwoods overlap heavily with AQA. Adapt the AQA timber lesson. Eduqas 2024 examiner report flagged Natural and Manufactured Timbers as the most popular Question 6 — this lesson must be a flagship in terms of depth and exam-style practice.

lessons.title: Ferrous and Non-Ferrous Metals
lessons.description: Metal categorisation, properties, alloys, stock forms and protective finishes.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Metals categorisation, named alloys and working properties are universal D&T content. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt directly. Ensure tensile strength, malleability, ductility are foregrounded — Eduqas amplification lists these explicitly.

lessons.title: Thermoforming and Thermosetting Polymers
lessons.description: Polythene, polystyrene, polypropylene, PVC and the thermosetting plastics UF, MF, PR and ER.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Polymer categorisation and named examples are universal. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt directly. Spotlight Eduqas examiner note: few candidates select polymers as their in-depth material — those who do need to demonstrate breadth beyond the obvious 'PET bottle' examples.

lessons.title: Natural and Synthetic Textiles
lessons.description: Animal, insect, plant and synthetic fibres. Blends, mixes and the properties that matter for fabric choice.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Fibre sources and categorisations are universal. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt directly. Eduqas amplification names microfibres Tactel and Tencel explicitly — must appear in flashcards and glossary.

lessons.title: Woven, Non-Woven and Knitted Textile Construction
lessons.description: Plain, twill and satin weaves, felts and bonded fabrics, and warp and weft knits.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA D&T covers fabric construction at lower depth in its specialist textiles lesson. Eduqas gives this a dedicated content strand within in-depth fibres and textiles. Expand from any AQA source with fresh structural illustration of warp/weft and a properties-vs-construction table. May need to generate ~half fresh.

article_units.name: Designing and Making Principles
article_units.subtitle: User needs, design strategies, communicating ideas, prototypes and the work of designers

lessons.title: Context, User Needs and Design Briefs
lessons.description: Investigating contexts, primary and secondary research, design briefs and writing specifications.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Design brief and specification writing concepts are universal. AQA D&T has an analogous lesson in Designing & Making. Adapt directly. Note: this content is exam-only (no NEA-specific guidance in revision content).

lessons.title: Investigating the Work of Designers and Companies
lessons.description: Airbus, Apple, James Dyson, Philippe Starck and Matthew Williamson — how their work informs design decisions.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Eduqas specifies five named designers/companies (Airbus, Apple, Dyson, Starck, Williamson). AQA D&T does NOT mandate the same five designers — its designer-focus content uses different exemplars. Content agent must generate this lesson fresh, focused tightly on the Eduqas-mandated five. No reuse from AQA designer content.

lessons.title: Design Strategies and Avoiding Design Fixation
lessons.description: Collaboration, user-centred design, systems thinking and how to break out of design fixation.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Design-strategy taxonomy (collaboration, user-centred, systems thinking) is shared with AQA. Adapt directly. Surface Eduqas extended-writing emphasis on iterative design as a vehicle for examiner-rewarded responses.

lessons.title: Communicating Design Ideas
lessons.description: 2D and 3D drawing, schematic diagrams, exploded views, models and mathematical modelling.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Drawing conventions and visualisation methods are universal. AQA D&T has an equivalent lesson. Adapt directly.

lessons.title: Prototyping, Testing and Iterative Improvement
lessons.description: Developing a prototype, ergonomics, anthropometrics and acting on feedback from users.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Prototyping, ergonomics and feedback are universal D&T concepts. AQA D&T covers identically. Adapt directly. Eduqas examiner finding: good responses on benefits of user testing; weaker responses focus only on improving end product rather than informing design decisions throughout.

transferability_note: AQA D&T free-tier (slug 'design-technology', 20 lessons across 3 units) is the canonical source. Core technical principles, materials, mechanisms, smart materials and design strategies are largely universal across all D&T boards (~70%+ transferable). Eduqas-specific items requiring fresh or adapted treatment: the five named designers (Airbus, Apple, Dyson, Starck, Williamson), Eduqas-named technical textiles (Rhovyl, Tactel, Tencel, Nomex), in-depth mechanical calculations using the Eduqas RV*dia formula, and the Q6 in-depth material area exam framing (one extended response on a chosen material area). Per-lesson source_lesson_number is set to null and will be matched by content agents when they fetch the AQA lesson list.

unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: AQA D&T designer lesson uses different exemplars from Eduqas's prescribed five (Airbus, Apple, Dyson, Starck, Williamson). The AQA-specific designers do not appear in the Eduqas amplification and would not be examined here.

unique_to_target.unit: Design and Technology in Our World
unique_to_target.why_no_source_match: Eduqas elevates technical textiles to a dedicated content strand (Rhovyl, Nomex, geotextiles, interactive textiles, micro-fibres). AQA D&T treats these inside a more compressed smart-materials lesson. Eduqas requires fuller standalone treatment.

unique_to_target.lesson: Mechanical Calculations: Levers, Gears and Pulleys (L4)
unique_to_target.why_no_source_match: Eduqas spec contains explicit formulas (RV of driver*dia of driver = RV of driven*dia of driven; principle of moments for levers) and worked numerical examples are expected in Section A. AQA covers mechanical advantage less procedurally — this lesson needs Eduqas-style numerical worked examples embedded in the article format.

unique_to_target.lesson: Investigating the Work of Designers and Companies (L2)
unique_to_target.why_no_source_match: Eduqas mandates a specific list of five designers and companies (Airbus, Apple, Dyson, Starck, Williamson). This lesson must be generated fresh against that exact list.

question_type_names: 12 marks — Extended Response on Material Properties

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students write vague sustainability suggestions like 'make it more eco-friendly' rather than naming a specific action ('use recycled polymers' or 'design for disassembly'). Eduqas examiners explicitly contrast these two answer types and only credit the specific action.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students name a component like 'moisture sensor' without explaining the mechanism of detection. The examiner report notes superficial responses lose marks even when the component named is technically correct.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Candidates attempt more than one Q6 in the exam (the question requires ONE in-depth material area). The 2024 examiner report flagged this as a notable problem and only the first response is marked.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Until recently students lost marks on mechanism calculations through poor method; the 2024 report notes substantial improvement, but the underlying error remains: students forget to state the formula and units before plugging in numbers.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students assume friction is always undesirable and write blanket statements about 'reducing friction to improve efficiency'. In belt and pulley systems friction is required for the mechanism to function — its absence would cause slip.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR GCSE Design and Technology Technical Understanding guidance, ocr.org.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students explain user testing only in terms of improving the final product, missing that feedback informs design decisions throughout the iterative process. Eduqas examiners want decision-influencing examples.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

common_misconceptions.misconception: Natural and manufactured timber is by far the most popular Q6 selection; very few candidates choose polymers, metals or electronic systems. Students who do choose those underused areas often demonstrate shallower depth, suggesting their teaching coverage is narrower.
common_misconceptions.source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Examiners' Report Summer 2024, eduqas.co.uk

student_errors_by_question_type.3 marks — Calculate: Show working but always boxed final answer with units (mm, N, gsm, ratio). Formula alone scores zero in Eduqas — must reach a numerical answer. Source: Eduqas examiner commentary.
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Explain with Application: Generic explanations that don't reference the stimulus context lose marks. Students need to embed product or material context (e.g. 'because the kettle handle uses an insulating thermoset…') in at least one developed point. Source: Eduqas examiner commentary.
student_errors_by_question_type.8 marks — Discuss Advantages and Disadva: Students list points in two columns without weighing them. Eduqas levels-based mark scheme rewards balance and judgement, not symmetry. Source: Eduqas Sample Assessment Materials.
student_errors_by_question_type.12 marks — Extended Response on Material: Q6 is the in-depth material extended response. Top-band responses use specific named materials, processes and applications — generic 'metals are strong' answers stall in the lower band. Rubric requires ONE Q6 — answering two is the most-flagged 2024 error. Source: Eduqas examiner report 2024.

topic_weighting_notes: The written exam is 100 marks over 2 hours, 50% of qualification. Structure (per Eduqas Sample Assessment Materials): Q1 10m, Q2 10m, Q3 15m, Q4 20m, Q5 20m, plus ONE Q6 of 25m on a chosen in-depth material area.
Section A (Q1-5, 75 marks) covers core technical principles + designing and making principles — these get the bulk of revision time.

Section B (Q6, 25 marks) is a single extended response on the candidate's chosen in-depth material area. Students choose one of: electronic systems, papers and boards, timber, metals, polymers, fibres and textiles. We treat papers and boards, timber, metals, polymers and textiles as compulsory lessons because students may have studied any of these.

AO weighting for the written exam: AO3 = 10% of total qualification (analyse and evaluate wider issues), AO4 = 40% of total qualification (knowledge and understanding of technical principles and designing principles). Source: Eduqas specification page 35.
Mathematical content carries explicit weighting (Appendix B of spec): percentages, ratios, area/volume, scaling, basic algebra, principle of moments, gear/pulley ratio calculations.
The named-designer content (Airbus, Apple, Dyson, Starck, Williamson) is small in mark weight but explicitly listed in the spec — must be covered.
current_spec_changes: No content changes since Specification Version 2 (January 2019). Awards continue under the same regulations as first award 2019. Source: Eduqas GCSE Design and Technology Specification Version 2, eduqas.co.uk.
pedagogical_notes: EEF guidance on cognitive load (Working with Worked Examples, 2023) emphasises that complex procedures should be modelled step-by-step before students attempt independent calculation. Apply this to mechanical-calculation lessons: present the formula, work an example fully, then fade scaffolding for practice questions. Source: educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk.

EEF science research notes that worked examples are particularly powerful for transfer in STEM domains, which D&T calculations sit within. Source: educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk, 'Ways into Science — making the most of worked examples'.

Eduqas Sample Assessment Materials show Q6 stems are open-ended ('Discuss the use of [material] in [context]') — students benefit from rehearsal with paragraph-level exemplars at each rubric tier (Mastering/Secure/Developing/Emerging). Source: Eduqas SAMs.

Cambridge Assessment research on levels-based mark schemes (Macinska & Benton 2020) shows examiner agreement is highest where students see exemplar paragraphs at each tier, not band descriptors alone — embed these into the extended-response exam tips. Source: cambridgeassessment.org.uk.

Tes practitioner consensus on D&T technical content: knowledge organisers paired with quick-recall flashcards (especially for named materials, properties tables and stock forms) build the technical vocabulary students need before they can write extended responses. Source: tes.com (style and structure reference only).
